utterance: The `shared-scratch-vpc` VPC (10.0.0.0/16) is already in the account with two private subnets in it, 10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24, and so is the EFS file system `my-efs`, which no subnet can reach yet. Set that file system up as shared storage for two servers: create a security group named `ec2_sg` in the VPC that allows inbound TCP on 22, 80 and 2049 from 0.0.0.0/0 and all outbound traffic; give `my-efs` a mount target in each of the two private subnets, using that security group; set the file system to move files to Infrequent Access storage after 30 days; and launch 2 of the newest Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instances, t2.micro, one in each private subnet, on that security group, with user data that mounts `my-efs` at /mnt/efs.

main.responsibility: owns the application's resources and their configuration
main.intent: the pre-existing EFS file system my-efs carries a lifecycle configuration that transitions files to Infrequent Access after 30 days and has one mount target in each of the two pre-existing private subnets of the shared-scratch-vpc VPC; two new t2.micro EC2 instances run, one in each of those two subnets; and a security group in that VPC admits inbound TCP 2049, and both mount targets and both instances are on it
